title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
abstract: arXiv:2610.23257v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability, the ability of reasoning models to control properties of their CoT, is consequential for both their usefulness and reliable oversight. Recent work evaluates this capability by measuring whether models follow CoT constraints given in the user prompt, and reports very low controllability across models. We argue that this low controllability may not reflect an inherent inability of reasoning models to control their CoT, but instead result from naively specifying constraints in the user prompt. To test this, we introduce Self-Instructed CoT Controllability: a complementary evaluation that places the constraint as a self-instruction inside the model's CoT and measures its ability to follow it. We show that, under self-instruction, models achieve significantly higher controllability than with standard user instructions. translated_title: 推理模型在自我指令下能够控制其思维链
translated_abstract: 思维链（CoT）可控性，即推理模型控制其思维链属性的能力，对模型的有用性和可靠监督都具有重要意义。近期研究通过测量模型是否遵循用户提示中给出的CoT约束来评估这一能力，并报告各模型均表现出极低的可控性。我们认为，这种低可控性可能并非反映推理模型天生无法控制其CoT，而是源于在用户提示中简单直接地指定约束的方式。为验证这一点，我们提出了自我指令CoT可控性（Self-Instructed CoT Controllability）：一种互补的评估方法，它将约束作为自我指令置于模型的CoT内部，并测量模型遵循该约束的能力。我们表明，在自我指令条件下，模型实现的可控性显著高于标准用户指令下的水平。即使仅是提醒模型遵循用户约束的通用提示，也能大幅提升可控性。
tldr: 推理模型并非天生无法控制其思维链，将约束作为自我指令置于CoT内部时，模型的可控性显著优于在用户提示中指定约束的方式。
en_tdlr: Reasoning models are not inherently unable to control their chains of thought—placing constraints as self-instructions within the CoT yields significantly higher controllability than specifying them in the user prompt.
